indicators.name: Real GDP growth
indicators.basis: Mean of annual real GDP growth at constant prices, fiscal years (April-March) labelled by start year, as compiled by the World Bank from national accounts. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted). inc-pre-1991 takes only years under INC-led governments (observations for 1977-79 under the Janata/Charan Singh governments and 1990 under V. P. Singh/Chandra Shekhar are excluded from that mean); series start years limit this window.

source.title: World Bank WDI: GDP growth (annual %), India (derived from MoSPI/CSO national accounts)

caveats: Series mixes national-accounts vintages. As of this pull the latest fiscal years (FY2023-24 7.2, FY2024-25 7.1, FY2025-26 7.6) match MoSPI's new series with base year 2022-23 (released 27 Feb 2026; reported in search results, e.g. https://www.5paisa.com/blog/india-gdp-base-year-reset, not opened); earlier years follow the 2011-12 base series. Reports say growth for FY2023 and earlier is not directly comparable across the two bases and that a back series on the new base was expected later; modi2's mean includes FY2023-24 on the new base and modi3's mean is entirely new-base.

The 2011-12 base revision (2015) raised growth and changed methodology (MCA21 company data, GVA at basic prices). The back series for 2004-05 to 2011-12 published in 2018-19 and the growth figures for roughly 2011-12 to 2016-17 were publicly contested by some economists (e.g. an argument that growth was overstated by about 2.5 percentage points); the government and some other economists disputed that. Not re-verified in this session. The pre-2011-12 values here are from older base series (e.g. 1993-94, 1999-00, 2004-05) as carried by the World Bank, so cross-period comparison mixes bases.

Global events inside periods: 1991 balance-of-payments crisis (rao FY1991-92 growth 1.1%); 1997-98 Asian crisis and 1998 Pokhran sanctions (nda1); 2008-09 global financial crisis (upa1/upa2 boundary; FY2008 3.1% is the low); 2013 taper tantrum (upa2); 2014-16 oil price fall (modi1); 2020 COVID-19 (FY2020-21 -5.8%, modi2); 2022 energy shock after Russia-Ukraine war.
Pre-1991 years include the 1965-66 and 1972-73 droughts, the 1973-74 oil shock and the 1979-80 oil shock/drought (FY1979 is excluded from the INC mean because it falls in a non-INC government).

indicators.name: World real GDP growth (context)
indicators.basis: Mean of annual world real GDP growth (World Bank aggregate), calendar years. Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted). inc-pre-1991 takes only years under INC-led governments (observations for 1977-79 under the Janata/Charan Singh governments and 1990 under V. P. Singh/Chandra Shekhar are excluded from that mean); series start years limit this window.

source.title: World Bank WDI: GDP growth (annual %), World

caveats: Global context only, not an Indian outcome. Calendar-year world figures are compared against India's fiscal-year figures, so timing is offset by about a quarter.

Includes the 1974-75 oil shock, the 1991 recession, the 1997-98 Asian crisis, 2008-09 financial crisis (-1.3% in 2009), 2020 COVID (-2.9%) and the 2022 energy shock; World Bank revises these aggregates, so values may differ from other editions.
Emerging-market peer series were not pulled in this session; the world aggregate includes advanced economies.

indicators.name: Consumer price inflation
indicators.basis: Mean of annual average CPI inflation, calendar years, as compiled by the World Bank. Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted). inc-pre-1991 takes only years under INC-led governments (observations for 1977-79 under the Janata/Charan Singh governments and 1990 under V. P. Singh/Chandra Shekhar are excluded from that mean); series start years limit this window.

source.title: World Bank WDI: Inflation, consumer prices (annual %), India

caveats: The WDI page did not name the underlying index. Indian CPI has historically been the CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW, Labour Bureau) and, from the 2011-12 base, the all-India CPI (Combined, MoSPI) from 2011 or 2012; where the splice falls was not verified, so treat the series as a headline consumer-price measure with a possible index change around 2011-13.
CPI-IW weights an industrial-worker basket, over-represents food in older bases, and differs from CPI-Combined; the 2010-13 double-digit readings reflect food prices.

Global events: 1973-74 oil shock (calendar 1974 28.6%), 1979-80 oil shock, 1991 crisis and rupee devaluation (13.9% in 1991), 1998 food/onion price spike (13.2%), 2008-09 commodity spike, 2013 taper tantrum rupee depreciation, 2014-16 oil price fall which lowered inflation, 2020 COVID supply disruption and 2022 energy shock. Inflation-targeting (4% +/-2%) with RBI began in 2016, within modi1.

indicators.name: Centre's gross fiscal deficit
indicators.basis: Mean of annual Centre gross fiscal deficit as % of GDP (current-price GDP), fiscal years labelled by start year. Years 2024-25 are Revised Estimates and 2025-26 Budget Estimates in the August 2025 Handbook edition; later actuals were not checked. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted). inc-pre-1991 takes only years under INC-led governments (observations for 1977-79 under the Janata/Charan Singh governments and 1990 under V. P. Singh/Chandra Shekhar are excluded from that mean); series start years limit this window.

source.title: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy, Table 236: Select Fiscal Indicators of the Central Government (% of GDP), dated 29 Aug 2025

caveats: Centre only; states excluded (see RBI Table 238 for combined deficits). Ratios use GDP denominators from successive base series, so levels before and after 2011-12 are not strictly like for like.
modi3 mean uses FY2024-25 RE (4.75) and FY2025-26 BE (4.40), not outturns, and may be revised.

Definition changes: from 2020-21 the Centre brought some off-budget items (e.g. FCI food subsidy loans) on-budget, which raises the reported deficit; FY2020-21 (9.2%) reflects COVID-19 spending and revenue loss; FY2008-09 and 2009-10 reflect the global financial crisis stimulus and loan waiver/ subsidies. FY1991-92 deficit fell in the 1991 stabilisation. Other reclassifications were not checked in this session.
Oil: under-recoveries/subsidies in 2005-13 affected the deficit; 2022 energy shock increased fertiliser/food subsidies.

indicators.name: Centre's outstanding liabilities (debt)
indicators.basis: Mean of end-March Centre total liabilities (domestic + external) as % of GDP, fiscal years labelled by start year. Series begins 1984-85; 2023-24 is Revised and 2024-25 Budget Estimate in the August 2025 edition. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted). inc-pre-1991 takes only years under INC-led governments (observations for 1977-79 under the Janata/Charan Singh governments and 1990 under V. P. Singh/Chandra Shekhar are excluded from that mean); series start years limit this window.

source.title: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy, Table 239: Select Debt Indicators of Central and State Governments (% of GDP), dated 29 Aug 2025

caveats: Includes securities/treasury bills under the Market Stabilisation Scheme; external debt is valued at current exchange rates, so rupee depreciation raises measured external liabilities (e.g. 1991-92, 2013).

modi3 mean is a single year (FY2024-25 BE, 56.82). A 40% central-debt ceiling under the FRBM framework for 2024-25 was cited in a fact-check explainer seen in search results (https://factly.in/explainer-understanding-government-debt, not opened); the reported ratio is above that.

FY2020-21 jump (62.6%) reflects COVID-19 borrowing and a GDP contraction in the denominator. 1991 crisis, 2008-09 crisis and 2022 energy shock all affected borrowing needs. Inc-pre-1991 mean covers FY1984-89 only.

values.note: Mean of 1 of 2 years: 2024-25 to 2024-25 (missing years: 2025-26)

indicators.name: Current account balance
indicators.basis: Mean of annual balance of payments current account balance as % of GDP, calendar years (World Bank). Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: World Bank WDI: Current account balance (% of GDP), India

caveats: Series starts 1990 in the pull; inc-pre-1991 omitted. Equal-weighted calendar-year means.

Global events: 1991 BoP crisis, 1997-98 Asian crisis, FY2008-09 oil and capital reversal, the 2012 peak deficit (-5.0%) before the 2013 taper tantrum, oil price collapse 2014-16 narrowing deficits, 2020 COVID import compression (surplus 1.2%), 2022 energy shock (-2.4%).
BoP definitions were revised (BPM5 to BPM6 in 2012-13) and data are revised by RBI; World Bank values may differ slightly from RBI's fiscal-year figures.

indicators.name: Gross FDI inflows
indicators.basis: Mean of annual gross inflows of foreign direct investment (RBI 'Gross Inflows': direct investment to India before repatriation/disinvestment), fiscal years labelled by start year. Series begins 2004-05; 2025-26 provisional. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy, Table 143: Foreign Investment Inflows, dated 31 Jul 2026

caveats: Earlier periods (rao, nda1) omitted because the fetched RBI table starts in 2004-05 and FDI definitions were revised in 2000-01; not spliced.

Current US dollars, not inflation-adjusted, so later periods are inflated by price and GDP growth. FDI data were revised since 2000-01 to include reinvested earnings and other capital, and from 1995-96 include acquisitions of shares under FEMA; 2006-07 includes a US$3.1bn share swap.
Gross inflows differ from DPIIT's equity-inflow factsheet series, which have narrower coverage.

Global events: FY2008-09 financial crisis, 2013 taper tantrum, 2020 COVID, 2022 monetary tightening. Rising repatriation/disinvestment in recent years sharply narrows net figures (see net indicators).

indicators.name: Net FDI inflows to India (balance of payments)
indicators.basis: Mean of annual net inward FDI (inflows less disinvestment/repatriation by non-residents), calendar years, current US$, as compiled by the World Bank from BoP data. Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: World Bank WDI: Foreign direct investment, net inflows (BoP, current US$), India

caveats: This is net of repatriation but before India's own outward FDI (see 'Net FDI after outward investment'). It tracks RBI's 'Direct Investment to India' (e.g. 2023 27.1 vs RBI FY2023-24 26.8).
Current US dollars. Definitions were revised around 2000-01 and with BPM6, so the pre- and post-2000 values are not strictly like for like.
Global events: 1991 crisis and liberalisation start from a very low base; 2008-09 crisis; 2013 taper tantrum; 2020 COVID; 2022-24 rising repatriation.

indicators.name: Net FDI after outward investment
indicators.basis: Mean of annual RBI 'Net FDI' (direct investment to India net of repatriation, less FDI by India abroad), fiscal years labelled by start year. Series begins 2004-05; 2025-26 provisional. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy, Table 143: Foreign Investment Inflows, dated 31 Jul 2026

caveats: Net FDI fell to US$1.0bn in FY2024-25 as repatriation and outward investment rose; modi3 mean covers FY2024-25 and the provisional FY2025-26 only.
Current US dollars; definitions as for gross FDI; earlier periods omitted rather than spliced.

indicators.name: Merchandise exports
indicators.basis: Mean of annual merchandise exports in current US$, calendar years (World Bank, from trade statistics). Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: World Bank WDI: Merchandise exports (current US$), India

caveats: Current US dollars, not adjusted for inflation; values are calendar-year and differ from the Commerce Ministry's fiscal-year customs data and RBI's BoP figures. Not cross-checked against the Commerce Ministry in this session.

Exports exclude services. Global events: 1991 crisis, 1997-98 Asian crisis, 2008-09 collapse in world trade, 2014-16 fall in petroleum product prices (2015-16 exports fell), 2020 COVID (276bn), 2021-22 rebound and 2022 energy shock (higher petroleum export prices).

indicators.name: Foreign exchange reserves at end of period
indicators.basis: Total reserves including gold, current US$, as at the last calendar year-end (December) on or before the period's end date; modi3 is the latest year-end in the dataset (December 2025), not the current level. Not an average.

source.title: World Bank WDI: Total reserves (includes gold, current US$), India

caveats: Year-end dates are December, not the actual government end date (e.g. Rao period ends May 1996, so December 1995 is used). RBI's March and weekly figures differ.
Includes gold valued at market prices, so changes partly reflect gold price and exchange-rate valuation effects, not only inflows.
Context: 1991 reserves covered about two weeks of imports (reserves of US$5.6bn at end-1990); 2008 outflows, 2013 taper tantrum and 2022 dollar strength lowered reserves temporarily.

indicators.name: Unemployment rate (PLFS, usual status)
indicators.basis: Mean of annual PLFS usual status (ps+ss) unemployment rate, persons age 15+, all-India rural+urban, July-June survey years labelled by starting year (2017-18 = 2017). Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: MoSPI Press Note: PLFS Annual Report July 2023 - June 2024 (Table 3)

caveats: PLFS began in 2017-18; earlier NSSO employment-unemployment surveys used a different design and are not spliced, so earlier periods are blank.
nda2-modi1 covers only FY2017-18 and 2018-19 (2 of 5 years). modi3 is blank: a calendar-2025 usual-status rate of 3.1% was seen in a search snippet, not verified or on the same July-June basis.

Usual status ps+ss counts anyone with subsidiary work in the year as employed, which gives low rates; current weekly status rates are higher (see Table 6 of the report). The 2020-21 survey year spans COVID-19.

indicators.name: Unemployment rate (ILO modelled estimate, context)
indicators.basis: Mean of annual ILO modelled estimates of total unemployment, calendar years (World Bank WDI). Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: World Bank WDI: Unemployment, total (% of labour force) (modeled ILO estimate), India

caveats: Modelled series, not a survey result; it is almost flat at about 7.6% from 1991 to 2018 and then falls from 2019, which is consistent with the model switching to PLFS survey inputs; the cause was not verified, so treat the step change with caution. Not comparable with PLFS usual-status rates.
Provided only so every period has some labour-market measure on one basis; the PLFS series is the official source.

indicators.name: Brent crude oil price (global context)
indicators.basis: Mean of annual average Brent spot prices, nominal US$, calendar years (IMF series via FRED). Series begins 1992, so rao covers 1992-95 only. Calendar-year labels. Periods are assigned annual observations by this rule: a year is counted in a period if the midpoint of that year (1 October for a fiscal year April-March, 1 July for a calendar year) falls within the government's term per src/data/governments.json; fiscal years are labelled by starting year (e.g. 2014 = FY2014-15). Period value is the simple arithmetic mean of those annual values (not GDP- or time-weighted).

source.title: FRED / IMF: Global price of Brent Crude (POILBREUSDA)
source.publisher: IMF via Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

caveats: Nominal, not inflation-adjusted. Global context, not a policy outcome; India imports most of its crude so prices feed into inflation, the current account and subsidies.

Events: 1998 price low, 2008 spike and crash, 2011-14 prices above US$100, 2014-16 oil price fall, 2020 COVID demand collapse, 2022 energy shock after the Russia-Ukraine war. Pre-1991 shocks (1973, 1979) are not covered by this series.

values.note: Mean of 4 of 5 years: 1992 to 1995 (missing years: 1991)
